demos.heading: Before you run anything: set up the shell
demos.purpose: DocuMind can answer a tenant's questions from four stores: its own Vector Search index (the ANN tier), the Firestore rung beneath it, or two managed mirrors, Vertex AI RAG Engine and Vertex AI Search. make up pins acme to RAG Engine and zeta to Vertex AI Search so every store the course teaches is exercised. A managed store holds the text of every current version, but not the kit's addresses: its citations come back with ids like acme:acme_497809ff...#rag-532341da71fe, a page of null even for a PDF, and stages.retrieval_backend: rag_engine. This lesson is about the kit's own rows, so point acme at them for the duration and put the pin back at the end. Module 2 compares the four stores; Module 7 studies the mirrors.

demos.heading: The decision eval for Rs 0, a higher floor, and Jev's switch
demos.purpose: Do it: all 65 rows, Rs 0 Raise the floor and the rule buys refusals with answers. The same run at 0.70: shared/system_one.py is the only door to Jev, and decide() its only entry point. It never raises: every outcome is a result with a verdict of answer, refuse, skipped or error, and only the first two are decisions. The mode is read at call time, and off returns at once. An empty pool is refused in code, as rag-api refuses it, before any mode could ask Jev. Recorded mode reads the recorded file and nothing else. Live mode checks the tenant's data_region first, failing closed to in, then builds the payload from the question and the passages' text with identifiers masked, and only then reaches the adapter seam: _headers(), _request() and _parse(), which PR 2.6-C fills once TypeSafe documents its API. Until then _request() raises before any key is read or any socket opens, and decide() turns that into an error row, which no rate counts as a refusal. Run the Rs 0 eval with JEV_MODE=recorded on zeta's 10 rows, then call decide() in each mode, with the data regions make roster writes standing in for the Firestore read:
